findings.body:
**Check queue compatibility after `runner_units_stopped`, not before it.**

`compatibility_record(effects, record["prior_head"])` at Line 1846 reads `queue.json` before Line 1852 confirms that the runner units are inactive. A tick that is still finishing can add an `author_*` key between those two lines. `state` is captured after the stop (Line 1857), so `preservation_check` treats the new queue as the baseline. The rollback then installs a prior target that has not been shown to read that queue.

`deploy_plan` avoids this problem because it recomputes compatibility after the switch. Move the live check after the unit fence and the drain.

<details>
<summary>Proposed reorder</summary>

```diff
-        live_compatibility = compatibility_record(effects, record["prior_head"])
-        if not rollback_compatible(live_compatibility):
-            raise Refused(...)
         runner_units_stopped(helper_module, effects.root)
         drain = drain_check(effects, _runner_liveness(effects))
         if not drain["drained"]:
             raise Refused(...)
+        live_compatibility = compatibility_record(effects, record["prior_head"])
+        if not rollback_compatible(live_compatibility):
+            raise Refused(...)
         state = captured_state(effects)
```
</details>
findings.title: Check queue compatibility after `runnerunitsstopped`, not before it.

findings.body:
**`heartbeat.json` preservation hashes a path the runner never writes.**

`PRESERVED["heartbeat.json"]` resolves under `Effects.state_dir()`, which is `apps/crq-python/state`. The runner writes its completion heartbeat to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/crq/heartbeat.json` (or `~/.local/state/crq/heartbeat.json`), and `read_completion_heartbeat` reads that same path. `captured_state`, `no_change_observation`, and `preservation_check` all hash the state-relative path. Nothing in the runner writes it, so the entry is `None` before and after in normal operation. The check passes without comparing the real heartbeat. The module docstring states that the heartbeat is byte-identical, but no code enforces that. The docstring also lists receipts/claims, which `PRESERVED` does not hash.

Hash the heartbeat at the path `read_completion_heartbeat` reads, in all three sites. Expose that path through the `Effects` seam so injected test `Effects` keep control of the location. Do not only delete the entry. The docstring and `HOST-DEPLOY.md` state a byte-identity contract for the heartbeat, and removing the key changes the record schema that tests assert (`test_deploy_controller_first_tick.py:134`, `test_deploy_controller_unit_switch.py:494-501`). `HOST-DEPLOY.md:242` names `state/heartbeat.json`, which has the same path error. Its line 269 names the XDG path. Correct the docstring for any surface that stays unhashed.
findings.title: `heartbeat.json` preservation hashes a path the runner never writes.

**Move the resolved "code gap" items out of the open-defect list.**

Item 2 says the unfinished guard is one-sided and cites `refuse_unfinished_unit_switches` at `deploy-controller.py:1324-1333`. That function no longer exists in the file. The guard that now covers checkout and unit-switch records is `refuse_unfinished_transactions`, defined at `deploy-controller.py:1615`. The "Implemented" paragraph after item 4 describes this change.

Items 1-4 still read as open defects. Mark them as the pre-change finding. Keep only the gaps that remain open in the remaining-gaps list. Items 2 and 3 are resolved by the implemented guard and `recover_unit`, which now calls the same guard with `exclude=path`.

Also correct the line references. `recover_unit` is at `deploy-controller.py:1313`, not `1271-1320`. `controller_lock` is at `deploy-controller.py:228`, not `215-226`.
